candidats.description: Ziwei Palace is a single eave structure, with the hip and gable roof covered with yellow glazed tiles. In the middle of the roof is a gem tower with two Chiweis on both ends. The upward turning eaves splitting into two seperate ridges with beastlike figures on top.

candidats.description: Going down Westbourne Road in Edgbaston. This is the City South Campus of Birmingham City University in Edgbaston. Also known as Westbourne Campus. I once went here when it was the UCE, in the previous building (when I was in my last years of Primary School for a day - can't recall why we went here though). Before the UCE, it was the Birmingham Polytechnic Campus in Edgbaston. Lodge near the University. Grade II listed. candidats.description: Klein Noordijk estate: plastered square building with basement, two floors and an attic under a flat hipped roof coverde with muffled Old Dutch tiles. The centre bay of the front on the west side, facing the HW Iordensweg has a pointed gable extended just below the roof ridge and a gable roof with air springs with a profiled shelf, crowned by a gable sign. Nationally listed heritage.

Quatre branches diagonales, ou grands arêtiers, qui reçoivent ceux de remplissage, sont réunis à leur rencontre, dans le centre, au moyen d’un noyau en fer qui sert de clef et porte un tirefond. candidats.titre: File:The Baptist Church, Yardley Road, Acocks Green (4323860150).jpg
candidats.description: This is the Baptist Church on the Yardley Road in Acocks Green. The church related to the nearby church halls. I also spotted this on the bus going towards old Yardley a few weeks ago, and had to come back to capture it. It is a Grade II listed building dating from 1913. (It is 10 years younger than the 1903 Baptist Church Hall on Alexander Road round the corner). Baptist church. 1913, by F.B. Andrews for the Baptist Chapel Trustees. candidats.description: This is the mansion at Bletchley Park. Also known as Bletchley Park Mansion. It is Grade II listed. Large house, now offices. 1860 altered and extended 1883-6 and c1906 for HS Leon. Red brick in Flemish bond with ashlar dressings; principal gables half-timbered with pebble-dashed infill, some others tile-hung; Welsh slate roof with red tile ridge; brick stacks, with clustered flues, ribs and bands. Transomed wooden windows, principal windows with leaded upper lights. Decorative wooden barge boards and finials to gables. Large rambling house, of 2 storeys with partial attic. Entrance elevation:
